overall: The AG found the Douglas Conservation Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by entering executive session without a valid stated purpose, discussing staff professional competence and Stormwater Bylaw strategy in executive session. No remedy was ordered because the conduct predated July 1, 2010; the AG only encouraged future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the commission held executive session on May 4, 2010 without 48-hour notice to three staff members who were its subject. The letter did not separately rule on notice.
allegations.key_passage: This, by itself, is a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the commission entered executive session on May 4, 2010 'to discuss staff' for an improper purpose. The minutes gave no enumerated statutory purpose.
allegations.key_passage: On May 4, 2010, the Commission entered into executive session without citing one of the nine purposes available to it under G.L. c. 39 § 23B.

allegations.summary: Whether the executive session discussion of staff job performance and professional competence was a permitted purpose under the law.
allegations.key_passage: discussions about professional competence during executive sessions are explicitly prohibited by the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Commission discussed strategy for moving forward with the Stormwater Bylaw in executive session, which the letter found was not a proper executive session topic.
allegations.key_passage: In addition, the further discussion regarding strategy for proceeding with the Stormwater Bylaw was not appropriate for executive session.

allegations.summary: The letter found the May 4, 2010 executive session minutes, which recorded only one line of discussion, would not satisfy the current requirement for a summary of discussions.
allegations.key_passage: The executive session minutes from May 4, 2010 would not be sufficient to meet this requirement.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
